title: Lisse internal modules over pulled-back condensed coefficients
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme with small pro-etale site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Put $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. A $\Lambda_X$-module object $M$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] is lisse if there exists a pro-etale covering $\{U_i\to X\}$ such that, on each slice site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], $M|_{U_i}$ is isomorphic to $(\Lambda_X|_{U_i})^{r_i}$ for some $r_i\in\mathbf N$. The exponent denotes the finite direct sum of copies of the regular module, with $r_i=0$ allowed. The ranks may vary with $i$; no connectedness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: introductory paragraph: lisse means locally free of finite rank for the pro-etale topology; the coefficient-finite-descent-lisse statement and its conventions use exactly this notion
